titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 17, part 2
part: Spell 17, part 2 — Min's plumes, the double nest and the gates (Plates 7–8)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plates VII, VIII. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 32–36; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: The second part of Spell 17 goes on with the dead man's statements and their commentary: he is Min wearing two plumes, he drives out his wrongs, he is purified in the double nest of Herakleopolis, he passes the gates of Rosetau and of the supports of Shu, and he asks the gods in the presence for their arms. After each statement a question in red ("What, then, is it?") brings in a gloss, often with further glosses introduced by "another saying". On the papyrus it runs from Plate 7, line 30, to Plate 8, line 70, and it ends with the statement that Ani raised up the hair at the time of the storm, which the next part explains.

sentences.i: I am Min in his coming forth; I have set his two plumes upon my head.
sentences.n: A new statement. mnw 'Min' is the emblem of Min on a standard (coded R22 over R12; the drawing is uncertain in the print) with a seated god, as in the address to the gods after Spell 125 (Budge: Àmsu). prw·f 'his coming forth' is the house pr with r as complement, the chick w, walking legs and plural strokes, and ·f with its horns printed as a small cross: the noun prw from pri 'go forth', a god's appearing in procession. The top sign is a long flat rectangle in the print, taken as the house. iw opens the clause and is not translated. rdi·n·i 'I have set' is the mouth r and the giving arm di, then water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f with ·i. Budge takes it as a passive, 'may be given to me'; read rdi n·i, 'were given to me', the signs allow that too. šwty·f 'his two plumes' is the feather šw (H6), t and two oblique strokes y, the dual ending, with a tall double plume (coded S9) as classifier, and ·f; Budge's numeral 31 is printed inside the word. m tp·i 'upon my head': the owl m, the head with its stroke and ·i. Min of Coptos wears a crown of two tall plumes: to put on his plumes is to take his form.

sentences.i: As for Min, he is Horus, who protects his father.
sentences.n: ir 'as for' puts Min first as the topic, and ḥr pw 'it is Horus' answers. nḏ-ḥr 'who protects' is the sign nḏ, a knobbed staff (coded Aa27, approximate), with the pot nw standing for its n and a low sign (U15) as classifier, then the face ḥr with its stroke; Budge's numeral 32 is printed before the face. nḏ ḥr, with ḥr 'face', is 'protect, look after', and nḏ-ḥr itf·f 'who protects his father' is the participle (Budge: net'-ḥrà, 'the avenger of'). itf·f 'his father' is the reed, t and the viper f with its horns, a seated man (coded A1, as in part 1; the type draws it like the god's figure) and ·f. Min, the god of Coptos, was taken as a form of Horus, the son who stands up for his dead father Osiris.

sentences.i: As for his two plumes upon his head, that is the going of Isis and Nephthys: they have placed it(?) upon his head.
sentences.n: šwty·f 'his two plumes' is written here with the chick w after the feather, its complement; Budge's numeral 33 is printed inside it. šmt 'the going' is the pool with walking legs through it (N40, the sign šm) with m as complement, t and walking legs: the infinitive of šm 'go', with Isis and Nephthys after it as its subject; no pw is written. ꜣst 'Isis' is the seat ꜣs with t, the egg and a cobra as classifiers. ḥnꜥ 'and, together with'. nbt-ḥwt 'Nephthys' is the basket on the house (coded O9, approximate) with a cobra. Budge's three groups erṭā, en and sen are joined here as rdi·n·sn 'they placed': the mouth and the giving arm, the n of the sḏm·n·f, and ·sn (the bolt, water n and plural strokes). sw 'him, it' is the singular dependent pronoun, the object of rdi; what it stands for is not clear, and it cannot by itself mean 'themselves', Budge's rendering. The translation keeps 'it' with a query. ḥr-tp·f 'upon his head' is the face ḥr with r, then t and a small coil (coded Z7), which are not read, the head with its stroke, and ·f (Budge: ḥert-f); his numeral 34 is printed after the face. The two mourning sisters of Osiris become the two plumes of the crown.

sentences.i: They are there as the two kites, and they gather(?) over what ails his head.
sentences.n: wnn·sn 'they are' is the hare wn with water n twice (n as complement and the second n of wnn) and ·sn: the doubled stem of wnn 'be' (the sḏm·f), which may also look forward, 'they will be'. ḏrtw 'the kites' is the bundle ḏr (M36) with r as complement, t and the chick w each written twice, and two birds with long necks (coded G38, approximate): the signs are doubled for the pair, Isis and Nephthys as the two kites (Budge: t'ertutu, 'protectresses'). The second t and w are classifiers of the pair, not sounds. sꜣk·sn is the folded cloth s, the reed, the basket k and the vulture ꜣ (a crested bird in the print), with ·sn: read sꜣk 'gather, draw together', perhaps a writing of sꜣq 'gather', with the reed not read and ꜣ written after k (Budge: sàka-sen, 'they provide'); the reading is not sure. ḥr 'over' is the face with its stroke. mn is the gaming board mn with n, a small cross (coded Z9, printed above the bird) and the bird of bad things as classifiers: the noun 'ailment', from mn 'suffer', with tp·f 'his head' after it as a direct genitive. Kites crying over the dead are the image of the two sisters mourning Osiris.

sentences.i: Another saying: they are the two great and mighty uraei which are upon the head of their father Atum.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red (the small flat sign under the cobra is coded D46). ꜥrwt 'the uraei' is the arm ꜥ, r, w and t with two cobras as classifiers: iꜥrwt, the plural of iꜥrt 'uraeus', with its reed not written; the two cobras show the pair. wrt 'great' (the swallow wr with r and t) and ꜥꜣt 'great, mighty' (the column ꜥꜣ, laid flat in the print and coded O29, approximate, with ꜥ, t and the roll) agree with it in the feminine. A pw is 'they are A'. imyt 'which are upon' is the crossed planks im with m and t, the feminine of imy, its y not written. tp itf·sn 'the head of their father': tp with its stroke, itf with the seated man (A1) and ·sn. tm 'Atum' is t, the sledge and the owl with a god, as in part 1. Here the two sisters are the rearing cobras on the brow of the creator.

sentences.i: Another saying: his two plumes upon his head are his two eyes.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the whole gloss in red. Water n after ky ḏd has no clear place and is not translated. irty·f 'his two eyes' is the eye ir written twice, the second for the dual, with ·f: the dual of irt 'eye'. A pw B is 'B, they are A'. šwty·f 'his two plumes' with the chick w, as in line 32, and m tp·f 'upon his head'. sentences.l: Millions · the-name · of · the-one · Great-Green · the-name · of · the-other
sentences.i: 'Millions' is the name of the one, 'Great Green' is the name of the other.
sentences.n: ḥḥ 'Millions' is the kneeling god with raised arms (C11), the number a million, with two strokes (the second a thin dashed line in the print). A noun set before rn n X names X: 'Millions is the name of the one'. rn 'name' is the mouth and water n with the man with hand to mouth; wꜥ 'the one' is the harpoon with a stroke and the arm ꜥ as complement. Budge's two groups uat' and urà are joined here as wꜣḏ-wr 'the Great Green': the papyrus stem wꜣḏ (M14), the swallow wr with r, a reed that is not read (Budge's numeral 46 is printed before it), and three water lines over a pool as classifiers. ky 'the other' is the basket k and two reeds. The two nests are named for endless time and for the great water.

sentences.l: as-for · Rosetau · (pw) · the-gate · it-is · southern · of · En-iarered-ef · the-gate · northern · of · the-Mound
sentences.i: As for Rosetau, it is the southern gate of En-iarered-ef, the northern gate of the Mound.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes iꜣrrd-f; read n-iꜣrrd-f. rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'Rosetau' is the mouth rꜣ with a stroke, a coil on a stick (coded V2) for sṯꜣ, a stroke, plural strokes and the desert hills (coded N25, approximate), as in Spell 1. pw stands after the topic, as in ir nḥḥ pw in part 1, and again after the next noun. That noun, here and after the name, is the star N14 with ꜣ, w, t and the house sign (an open box, approximate). The star writes both sbꜣ 'gate' and dwꜣ in dwꜣt 'the Duat', and Budge reads the same signs ṭuaut, 'the underworld', the first time and sebaut, 'the door', the second; the pairing of south and north asks for the same word both times, read sbꜣwt 'gate'. The reading is not sure. rst 'southern' is the plant rs with t, the canal sign (approximate) and a stroke; mḥty 'northern' is the crown of the north mḥ with t and two strokes y. n-iꜣrrd-f 'En-iarered-ef' is written here without the n that the name has in the introduction to Spell 125; Budge too reads it with n (Naàrutf). The water n before it may instead be the n of the name, with the genitive not written; the sense is the same. What is written is the vulture and the reed (in that order), r, a cord with tails (coded T12, approximate) for rd, an open box (approximate) and the viper f with its horns, with the town sign. iꜣt 'the Mound' is the reed, ꜣ and t with a dome inside a frame (coded O20, approximate), a stroke and the canal sign. Rosetau, the cemetery land of Memphis, is here the passage between two holy places of Osiris.

sentences.i: I, the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice, have filled the Sound Eye for you after it was harmed(?),
sentences.n: A new statement; iw opens it. mḥ·n·i 'I have filled' is the crown of the north mḥ (V22), with a flat bar with a bowl on it (coded R4, approximate) as classifier, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i; the name and title after it stand beside ·i, 'I, the Osiris Ani'. ꜣny here ends with the seated man on a chair (A51). mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written with the sickle mꜣ before the plinth mꜣꜥ, the arm ꜥ and the oar. The papyrus writes n·k wḏꜣt in red: n with the basket ·k, 'for you', then wḏꜣt 'the Sound Eye', the wedjat: the chick w, a tall tapering sign ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate), ꜣ, t and the eye with the falcon's markings (D10). hꜣb·s is the courtyard h, ꜣ and the foot b with walking legs and the bird of bad things, and the bolt ·s, 'it', the Eye; Budge's numeral 66 is printed before the bird, he renders 'after it had failed', and he prints a plain h. A verb hꜣb with this sense is not otherwise known: the translation follows the classifier, and the reading is doubtful. To fill the Eye is to make it whole again, and every offering is an Eye of Horus restored.

sentences.i: It is that day on which Horus fought with Seth, when Seth cast filth(?) in the face of Horus and Horus seized the testicles of Seth.
sentences.n: hrw pwy 'that day', as in line 66: pwy, with two reeds, is the demonstrative. No pw 'it is' is written, and 'it is' is supplied in the translation, as in line 32; pwy may stand for pw, but that is not sure. ꜥḥꜣ as in line 66, with ḥr 'Horus' after it as its subject, im·f 'on it', the day, and ḥnꜥ stẖ 'with Seth'. stẖ 'Seth' is the bolt, t and a small hatched sign (coded N37, approximate), taken as the ẖ of the name (the sign that writes it here is not clear), with a god (Budge: Set). m wd 'in casting' is the chick w and the hand d (a flat sign in the print; it may be Y1) with a small cross and the low sign U15 as classifiers: the infinitive of wdi 'put, cast', after m; Seth, named before, is taken as its subject. stw 'filth(?)' is the folded cloth s and t with a cup-like sign (coded W10, approximate), a spiral (coded Z7, approximate) for w, and walking legs: the word read stꜣt in part 1, here without ꜣ (Budge: setau, 'excrement'); the reading is doubtful. m ḥr ḥr 'in the face of Horus'. iṯt is the tether ṯ on walking legs (the sign iṯ, coded as V13 and D54), t and the low sign U15: the infinitive of iṯi 'seize', with ḥr 'Horus' as its subject (Budge: θet, 'carried off'). ẖrwy 'the testicles' is the sign ẖr with r, w and two strokes y, the dual ending, and a pouch-shaped classifier (coded F51, approximate); Budge's numeral 69 is printed before it. In the struggle for the throne of Osiris each god maimed the other.

sentences.n: in with a noun and a participle singles out the doer: in ḏḥwty ir nn 'it was Thoth who did this'. ẖrt after in is the group of line 49, taken as grt 'now, and'. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on a standard with t, two strokes and a god. ir 'who did' is the eye alone, the participle of iri. nn 'this' is two sedges and two waters n, as in part 1. ḏbꜥw·f 'his fingers' is the finger ḏbꜥ (D50) written three times for the plural, with ·f, and two strokes after the suffix (Budge: t'ebā-f). ḏs·f 'himself': with his own fingers. sentences.i: I have raised up the hair at the time of the storm.
sentences.n: A new statement. The sign Aa15, m, that opens it has no clear place and is not translated. sṯs·n·i 'I have raised up' is the bolt s, then, after Budge's numeral 70, a crooked post (coded O30, approximate), here carrying ṯs as the post of wṯs 'lift' does, and the low sign U15 as the classifier of force, with the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i: written without the rope ṯ that sṯs has in line 56 and in part 1. šn 'the hair' is the cord šn (V7) with n and a lock of hair (D3) with plural strokes (Budge: śen). m tr 'at the time' is t, r, the reed and the stem tr with the sun as classifier: tr 'season, time'. nšny 'the storm' is water n, the pool š (with a double slash in the print), n and two strokes y, with the U15 classifier of force and the sky with falling rain (N4): from nšn 'rage' (Budge: neśeni, 'storms in the sky'). The part ends here; the question 'What, then, is it?' and its gloss begin the next part.

glossary.ḏd: ḏd — to say, speak (verb; ḏd in N "said by N", the formula that brings in a speech); ḏdt "words, speech" (noun from it)
glossary.iꜥrt: iꜥrt — uraeus, the rearing cobra on the brow of gods and kings (noun; plural iꜥrwt)
glossary.wr: wr — great (adjective); a great one, a great amount (noun)
glossary.ꜥꜣ: ꜥꜣ — great (adjective); (adverb) here, hither · a second word of the same spelling: donkey, ass (noun) · a third word of the same spelling: door, door-leaf (noun; iry-ꜥꜣ "doorkeeper") · also greatly, very (adverb, after an adjective or participle: ḥsy ꜥꜣ 'greatly favoured')
glossary.imy: imy — who/which is in (the nisba of m "in"; plural imyw)
glossary.itm: itm — Atum, 'the Complete One', the creator god of Heliopolis (god's name; Budge: Tem)
glossary.n: n — not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …'
glossary.irt: irt — eye (noun f.; dual irty 'the two eyes')
glossary.wsir: wsir — Osiris, god of the dead and king of the world below; Wsir N "the Osiris N", the dead person (god's name; Budge: Àusàr)
glossary.sš: sš — scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here) · also to write, draw, paint (verb; written with the scribe's palette) · also the noun 'writing, document, record' (noun m.) · also to open (a door), spread open (verb; said of doors and bolts) · a further word of the same spelling: nest (noun m.; written with the nest of young birds; dual sšwy)
glossary.ḥtp: ḥtp — to be content, at peace, to rest (verb); peace; offering (noun; m ḥtp "in peace")
glossary.nb: nb — lord, master, possessor (of); (adjective, after a noun) every, all
glossary.ꜣny: ꜣny — Ani, royal scribe of Thebes, for whom the papyrus was made (personal name)
glossary.mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)
glossary.tꜣ: tꜣ — to be hot; tꜣ-ib 'hot-tempered' · a second word of the same spelling: land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw 'lands'; dual tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt; tp tꜣ 'upon earth')
glossary.ii: ii — to come (verb; ii·n·i "I have come")
glossary.ꜣḫt: ꜣḫt — horizon (noun f.; the place where the sun rises and sets; written with the sun between two hills) · a second word of the same spelling: the season of inundation (noun f.)
glossary.ny: ny — of (the genitive adjective; written n, fem. nt, pl. nw): rꜣ n ꜥq "spell of entering"
glossary.dr: dr — to drive away, repel, subdue (verb)
glossary.iwt: iwt — wrong, wrongdoing (noun f.; cf. iwyt 'wrongdoing'; Budge: āut)
glossary.ḫsr: ḫsr — to drive away, dispel (evil, wrongs) (verb; Budge: χersek)
glossary.ḏw: ḏw — evil, bad; an evil deed (adjective, noun; written with the mountain ḏw)
glossary.šꜥd: šꜥd — to cut, cut off (verb; infinitive šꜥd 'a cutting')
glossary.sḏm·tw·f: sḏm·tw·f — the tw of the sḏm·tw·f, the passive or impersonal form ("one …", "… is done") (verb form; written after the verb, before its suffix)
glossary.ẖpꜣ: ẖpꜣ — navel, navel cord (noun m.; Budge: χapaa)
glossary.ḫr: ḫr — to fall (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: to, near, with (preposition; of persons) · also 'before' (ḫr nṯrw 'before the gods')
glossary.sḥri: sḥri — to remove, drive away, put far off (verb; causative of ḥri 'be far')
glossary.iry: iry — one who belongs to, keeper of (nisba of r "to"; iry ꜥꜣ "doorkeeper")
glossary.wꜥb: wꜥb — to be pure, clean; to purify oneself, bathe (verb); pure (adjective) · also wꜥb 'wab-priest', the 'pure one', a priest of the ordinary rank (noun) · also wꜥb 'purification, purity' (noun)
glossary.hrw: hrw — terror, dread · a second word of the same spelling: day (noun; plural hrww)
glossary.msi: msi — to give birth; (passive) to be born (verb)
glossary.nty: nty — who, which, that (relative adjective); as a noun "he who"
glossary.pwy: pwy — this, that (masculine demonstrative, after its noun; hrw pwy 'that day')
glossary.ꜥbt: ꜥbt — offering, offerings (noun f.; Budge: ābet; reading doubtful)
glossary.rḫyt: rḫyt — common folk, subjects (noun; written with the lapwing)
glossary.·s: ·s — she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)
glossary.ḥḥ: ḥḥ — a million, countless (number); Heh, the god of endlessness
glossary.wꜥ: wꜥ — one; (as a noun) one (of), someone
glossary.wꜣḏ-wr: wꜣḏ-wr — 'the Great Green', the sea or a great body of water; also a name given to waters and places of the world below (place name; Budge: Uat'-urà)
glossary.ḥsmn: ḥsmn — natron, the salt used for cleansing and purifying (noun m.; Budge: ḥesmen)
glossary.mꜥꜣt: mꜥꜣt — a word not identified, perhaps a substance or a place (noun f.; not Maat; reading and sense uncertain; Budge: Māāāat, 'nitre')
glossary.sm: sm — to go, make one's way (verb; a doubtful reading) · also sm 'sem-priest', who led the rites at the tomb (noun; often written with the leopard-skin sign)
glossary.wtt: wtt — to beget, engender (verb); the begotten one, offspring (passive participle used as a noun)
glossary.gr: gr — to be silent, still (verb) · a second word of nearly the same spelling: the particle grt 'now, moreover, indeed' · the particle grt apparently also written ẖrt, with the sign ẖr, after ir and in (reading not sure)
glossary.rꜥ: rꜥ — Ra, the sun-god (god's name; Budge: Rā) · also the sun; day (noun; rꜥ nb 'every day')
glossary.ḏs: ḏs — self (noun; with a suffix, ḏs·f 'himself, by himself, of his own accord')
glossary.š-mꜣꜥt: š-mꜣꜥt — 'the Lake of Maat', a sacred lake of the world below (place name; Budge: Śe-Maāat)
glossary.rꜣ-sṯꜣw: rꜣ-sṯꜣw — Rosetau, the Sokar necropolis realm near Giza
glossary.rsy: rsy — southern (nisba adjective, from rsw 'south'; feminine rsyt) · also the south (noun)
glossary.n-iꜣrrd-f: n-iꜣrrd-f — En-iarered-ef, a holy place of Osiris; the name looks like n rd·f "it does not grow" (?) (place name; reading uncertain; Budge: Àn-àarruṭ-f)
glossary.mḥtt: mḥtt — north (noun); northern (nisba adjective, feminine) · also mḥty, the masculine 'northern' (nisba adjective)
glossary.iꜣt: iꜣt — standard, the pole or perch carrying a god's emblem; mound (noun)
glossary.ꜣbḏw: ꜣbḏw — Abydos, the holy city of Osiris (place name; Budge: Àbṭu) · a second word of the same spelling: the abdju-fish (noun; a fish that swims before the sun's bark)
glossary.ḫft: ḫft — in front of, facing; in accordance with; at the time of, when (preposition; also before a verb form)
glossary.wḏꜣ: wḏꜣ — to proceed, go on, set out (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: to be sound, prosper (verb; ꜥnḫ wḏꜣ snb 'life, prosperity, health')
glossary.r: r — to, towards, into, at (preposition); with an infinitive "in order to"; with the sḏmt·f "until"; after an imperative, with a suffix (ir·k), "yourself, then" · a second word of the same spelling: goose, fowl (noun; the goose sign) · also against (of hostility: r·i 'against me'); concerning, about (r·f 'concerning him')
glossary.sḫt-iꜣrw: sḫt-iꜣrw — the Field of Reeds, the fertile land of the blessed dead (place name f.; sḫt 'field' + iꜣrw 'reeds'; Budge: Seχet-Àrui)
glossary.ḏfꜣw: ḏfꜣw — food, provisions (noun m.; often paired with kꜣw)
glossary.ḥꜣ: ḥꜣ — behind, around, about (preposition; Budge: ḥa)
glossary.kꜣri: kꜣri — shrine, chapel (noun m.; Budge: kerà)
glossary.ḏsr: ḏsr — holy, sacred, set apart (adjective; verb 'be holy, set apart'; Budge: sert, as in tꜣ-ḏsr, Ta-sert)
glossary.sṯsw: sṯsw — supports, props of the sky (?) (noun, plural; written like sṯs 'raise up'; the sense is doubtful)
glossary.šw: šw — empty, lacking, free (of) (adjective; verb šwi 'be empty') · a second word of the same spelling: Shu, god of the air, who holds up the sky (god's name; Budge: Śu)
glossary.dwꜣt: dwꜣt — the Duat, the underworld through which the sun and the dead pass by night (noun f.; place name; Budge: Ṭuat)
glossary.rꜣ: rꜣ — mouth; utterance, spell (noun; rꜣ n … "spell for …", the heading of a chapter) · also 'opening, door' (noun; rꜣ n 'the door of')
glossary.iꜣby: iꜣby — left, on the left hand; eastern (nisba adjective; fem. iꜣbt; written with the emblem of the East)
glossary.bꜣḥ: bꜣḥ — presence (noun; m-bꜣḥ 'in the presence of'; imyw-bꜣḥ 'those who are in the presence'; Budge: baḥ)
glossary.imi: imi — give! (imperative of rdi 'give') · also cause, let (before a sḏm·f: imi wn·i 'let me be'; with a passive, imi di·tw 'cause that there be given')
glossary.ꜥ: ꜥ — arm, hand (noun; dual ꜥwy "the two arms") · a second word of the same spelling: state, condition (noun)
glossary.·tn: ·tn — you, your (2nd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.ḫpr: ḫpr — to come into being, happen, become (verb)
glossary.ḥnn: ḥnn — phallus (noun m.; also written ḥnnw)
glossary.m-ḫt: m-ḫt — after, behind, in the following of (compound preposition: m 'in' + ḫt 'rear'; before a verb 'after he has …')
glossary.wꜣi: wꜣi — to go far, set out; wꜣi r with an infinitive 'to set about, be on the point of' (verb; Budge: ua)
glossary.ꜥḥꜥ: ꜥḥꜥ — to stand, stand up (verb); standing-place, stand, support (noun; plural ꜥḥꜥw) · also ꜥḥꜥ·n 'then', the auxiliary that opens a narrative sentence
glossary.·w: ·w — ending of the 3rd person masculine singular of the stative ('he is …ed'; often not written) · also the suffix pronoun of the 3rd person plural 'they' in later Egyptian, written w
glossary.ḫt: ḫt — thing, things, property (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: wood, tree, stick, a wooden board (noun m.) · a third word: stairway, terrace (?) (noun; written with the stairway sign; Budge: χet, 'steps') · a fourth word: rear, following (noun; m-ḫt 'after', imyw-ḫt 'those in the following of')
glossary.ḥw: ḥw — Hu, 'Utterance', the god of the creative, commanding word (god's name; Budge: Ḥu)
glossary.siꜣ: siꜣ — to perceive, recognise, discern (verb); Sia, the god of perception
glossary.ẖrt: ẖrt — what belongs to someone, affairs, concerns; possessions (noun) · ẖrt hrw 'the daily round, what belongs to the day'
glossary.mḥ: mḥ — to fill, fill up (verb; mḥ wḏꜣt 'fill the Eye', make it whole)
glossary.·k: ·k — you, your (2nd person masculine singular suffix pronoun; the basket sign)
glossary.wḏꜣt: wḏꜣt — the wedjat, the Sound Eye of Horus, made whole after Seth tore it; the type of every offering (noun; Budge: utchat)
glossary.hꜣb: hꜣb — to be harmed, suffer loss (?) (verb; not otherwise known in this sense, and not hꜣb 'send'; reading and meaning uncertain; Budge: hab)
glossary.rḥwy: rḥwy — the Two Companions, a name of Horus and Seth (dual noun; Budge: Reḥu)
glossary.stẖ: stẖ — Seth, god of storm and disorder, who murdered Osiris (god's name; written stẖ or swt; Budge: Sut)
glossary.wdi: wdi — to put, place, cast; to inflict (verb)
glossary.stꜣt: stꜣt — excrement (?) (noun; not otherwise known: the reading and sense follow Budge's setat, and are doubtful) · also written stw, without ꜣ
glossary.iṯi: iṯi — to take, seize, take possession of (verb 3ae-inf; participle iṯ 'who took')
glossary.in: in — by (naming the agent, as in ḏd in N "said by N"); (particle) it is … · a second word of the same spelling: to say, said (verb; normally after the words quoted: in·sn 'they say', in N 'says N'; in·k 'you said')
glossary.ḏḥwty: ḏḥwty — Thoth, the ibis god of writing, reckoning and wisdom, recorder of the judgement of the dead (god's name; Budge: Teḥuti)
glossary.nn: nn — not, there is not (negative particle; nn + noun 'there is no …'; nn + sḏm·f 'will not …', the negative of the future; nn with a sentence without a verb 'there is not, … is not') · a second word of the same spelling: these, those (demonstrative pronoun before its noun, in classical Egyptian joined to it by the genitive n, nn n X; in later texts also without it)
glossary.sṯs: sṯs — to raise up, lift; to extol, praise (verb; causative of ṯs 'raise')
glossary.šn: šn — to revile, curse(?) (verb; reading and sense uncertain, perhaps for šnṯ 'revile') · a second word of the same spelling: hair (noun; written with the cord šn and the lock of hair; Budge: śen)
glossary.nšny: nšny — storm, raging (noun; from nšn 'rage'; Budge: neśeni)
